a: Concurrency manages many tasks at once; parallelism runs them truly simultaneously on multiple cores.
A race condition is when result depends on uncontrolled timing of concurrent access to shared data.
A critical section is code that must not run concurrently on the same shared resource.
Lock contention is when threads wait a lot for the same lock, hurting performance.
async/await writes asynchronous code in a sequential style without blocking the thread.
Callback hell is deeply nested callbacks that are hard to read; promises/async help.
A Promise represents a future value: pending, fulfilled, or rejected.
A thread pool reuses a fixed set of worker threads to run tasks.
Processes isolate memory; threads share memory within a process and are lighter-weight.
CPython's GIL allows only one thread to execute Python bytecode at a time; use multiprocessing for CPU parallelism.
Message passing shares data by sending messages instead of shared memory (safer concurrency).
The actor model uses isolated actors that communicate only via messages.
An atomic operation completes indivisibly — no intermediate state is visible to others.
Event-driven systems react to events (I/O, clicks, messages) instead of tight polling loops.
Backpressure slows producers when consumers cannot keep up.
Fan-out splits work to many workers; fan-in merges their results.
